reason: Aphyllous means leafless: the stem, scape, raceme or pinna bears no leaves. It is handled the same way as 'ebracteate' (bract absent).

label: runcinate
definition: A pinnately lobed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's lobes or teeth being sharp and pointing backwards towards the base. NOTE: Child of FLOPO:0991157 pinnately lobed; the backward direction alone is PATO:0002237 retrorse.
reason: This is a standard leaf-division term (as in Taraxacum) with no term in PATO or FLOPO. A pinnately lobed term with a retrorse lobe term attached would lose the fact that the lobes are sharp.

label: eucamptodromous
definition: A branched quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's secondary veins curving upwards towards the margin and gradually fading out there without joining one another in prominent loops. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0001970 brochidodromous and PATO:0001969 craspedodromous (Hickey 1973).
reason: This is a Hickey venation class, alongside the venation terms PATO already has. PATO has brochidodromous but not eucamptodromous.

label: stellate-lepidote
definition: A scaly quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being covered with small peltate scales whose margins are divided into radiating, star-like arms. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991127 scurfy; lepidote alone is PATO:0001804 scaly (rule C235).
reason: This is a distinct kind of indumentum (the coat of hairs or scales), found in Croton, Elaeagnus and Bromeliaceae. It is made a term the same way stipitate-glandular was, rather than splitting it into scaly plus star-shaped.

label: tunicate
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bulb or corm by virtue of its being enclosed in one or more dry, membranous, papery or fibrous outer coats (tunics). NOTE: PO has no tunic class; an alternative is a FLOPO anatomy class 'tunic' with a presence rule.
reason: This is a standard term for bulbs and corms. There is no tunic part in PO, so no presence rule is possible.
This follows the rule for 'narrowed' (C172). PATO tapered already means gradually narrowing.

target: new: conjunction of two values (falciform PATO_0002215 and secund FLOPO:0991146)
reason: Moss leaves described this way are both sickle-curved and turned to one side; this is not a value halfway between the two. Both terms exist, so annotate both. 'when dry' goes to the specimen-condition pattern (06).

label: caducous
definition: A shedability quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's falling off or withering very early, soon after it has formed or opened. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991181 marcescent and PATO:0001731 deciduous (plant); PATO deciduous inheres in the shedding plant, not in the shed part.
reason: Stipules, scales, hairs and staminodes are described as falling very early. Neither PATO nor FLOPO has a term for an early-shed part. Label it with the commoner word 'caducous' and keep fugaceous as an exact synonym.
It means the cell or part is wider than long across the axis, which is a comparison of two dimensions. PATO elongated would lose the direction.
This is the negation of 'widened', which the last review mapped to increased width (C182).

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (part of the bearer: plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023 + low brightness PATO_0000327)
reason: This is the colour of the part's tip, so it uses the part-of-the-bearer slot with existing terms. When a hue is given ('reddish brown'), that colour replaces 'dark'.

label: incumbent
definition: A positional quality inhering in the cotyledons of an embryo by virtue of their lying with the back of one cotyledon against the radicle, which is folded along it. NOTE: Botany-specific (Brassicaceae); accumbent, the radicle against the cotyledon edges, is its sibling.
reason: This is a key character for telling Brassicaceae apart, with no PATO term. The rare use for anthers is a different sense; keep the class to the embryo, cotyledon and radicle.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (part of the bearer: margin + membranous FLOPO:0991046)
reason: The quality is membranous, and it applies to the margin of the bract, sheath or bracteole. 'narrowly' and 'broadly' are the width of that margin and belong in the record (RDF), not in a term.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (§2 continuum between two values: ovate FLOPO:0991024 and triangular PATO_0001875)
reason: A shape between two existing values, of the same kind as oblong-ovate.

Here it means reduced or small (auricle, annulus, central strand). Uses such as 'not well developed at anthesis' are about a stage and go to the stage slot. The phrase is vague, so mapping it to decreased size is a weak reading.
An underdeveloped bud, seed or cyme is a reduced one. PATO hypoplastic (fewer cells, a disease term) and vestigial (an evolutionary remnant) both claim more than the floras say.
Weeping branches bend and hang downwards, which is what PATO drooping means. PATO:0104035 pendent is for hanging by its own weight, and its comment sets it apart from the weak-support sense.
The opposite of 'obvious' (C324, conspicuous) and the same as 'obscure' (C174). Caudex/'at anthesis' goes to the stage slot.

label: abruptly narrowed
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's width decreasing suddenly, over a short distance, towards its apex or base. NOTE: Contrast with PATO:0001500 tapered (gradually narrowing); FLOPO:0991169 clawed is the special case of a base narrowed into a stalk.
reason: It cannot go under tapered, because tapered means gradual. Clawed covers only the base narrowing into a stalk.

label: gynobasic
definition: A positional quality inhering in a style by virtue of its arising from the base of the ovary, between its lobes, rather than from its apex. NOTE: Botany-specific (Boraginaceae, Lamiaceae).
reason: This is a standard and important feature of the style, with no term. 'gynobasic spikes' and stamens are transcription or bearer errors.
These are comparisons with another part ('as long as', 'shorter than', '1/3 the length of'), which are already covered by the relation and ratio patterns.
'Without a border' means different things on different organs: a paler edge on phyllaries, a moss leaf border, the free rim of a staminal tube. There is no border class whose absence it could state.
Tubiform means tube-shaped, which is an exact synonym of PATO tubular. 'tubiform-urceolate' is a compound of two values and goes to the continuum pattern.
Concrescent styles, stigmas, mericarps and nectaries are like parts grown together, which is connate. Where a different organ is named, use adnate FLOPO:0991129 instead.

label: hemiparasitic
definition: A trophic quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its being green and photosynthetic while drawing water and mineral nutrients from a host plant through haustoria. NOTE: Probably outside PATO's scope (a way of life of the plant), like FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic; PATO has no parasitic quality to serve as parent.
reason: A widely used way-of-life term for whole plants (Santalaceae, Orobanchaceae). Kept in FLOPO alongside epiphytic.
Obdeltate is a triangle attached at its narrow end, which is the FLOPO obtriangular class.

label: ternately compound
definition: A structural quality inhering in a compound leaf by virtue of its being divided into three parts, each of which may again be divided into three, so that the leaflets are borne in threes. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991161 trifoliolate (once ternate, three leaflets); the number of divisions ('2-3×-ternately') goes to the count pattern 03.
reason: Leaves divided into threes again and again (Thalictrum, Aquilegia) are not trifoliolate, and PATO has no ternate term.
A ball flattened along one axis is an oblate spheroid, the same reading as 'depressed-globose' (C170).
On fern rachises and pinnae, the gemmae are buds that sprout new plants. PO gemma (PO:0025614) is only for buds on a thallus, so it does not fit vascular plants.
A denuded stem is one bare of leaves. The other sense (basal ribs or veins bare of blade tissue along a leaf sinus) needs the part-of-the-bearer pattern and is left out of this rule.
